partners.mechanism_chain: WNK1 (HGNC:12712) —INCREASES→ Regulation of sodium-chloride cotransporter activity (REACT:R-HSA-173565); CLCN2 (HGNC:2383) —DECREASES→ Regulation of epithelial sodium channel activity (REACT:R-HSA-173573); Regulation of sodium-chloride cotransporter activity (REACT:R-HSA-173565) —LEADS_TO→ Hypertension (HP:0000822); Regulation of epithelial sodium channel activity (REACT:R-HSA-173573) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperkalemia (HP:0011333). Haploinsufficiency of CLCN2 and ANO1 disrupts normal ion transport and membrane potential regulation (n3), which in turn impairs the regulation of vascular smooth muscle contraction (n4). This dysregulation contributes to the hypertension seen in Familial hyperaldosteronism type II (n5) and the cerebrovascular abnormalities characteristic of Moyamoya disease 7 (n6).

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that pathogenic variants in CLCN2 and ANO1 exclusively cause one disease but not the other, or if the directionality of the functional impact (e.g., loss-of-function vs. gain-of-function) differs significantly between the two diseases for these genes, the proposed shared mechanism would be falsified. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in CLCN2 or ANO1 with a combined gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01 in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying a shared mechanistic link between Familial hyperaldosteronism type II and Moyamoya disease 7 could pave the way for novel therapeutic strategies targeting ion channel function or vascular smooth muscle regulation, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 2. pseudohypoaldosteronism type 2C  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.390)

Loss-of-function mutations in CLCN2 (pseudohypoaldosteronism type 2C) impair chloride channel function, impacting pathways that regulate epithelial sodium channel activity and leading to hyperkalemia. The convergence is on the shared biological pathways regulating ion transport and blood pressure homeostasis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a common population variant in either WNK1 or CLCN2 with a minor allele frequency >1% in gnomAD that is associated with either disease would challenge the causal role of these genes in these rare conditions. _(variant: chr1:117150000-117250000)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared and divergent roles of WNK1 and CLCN2 in ion transport offers potential therapeutic targets for managing hypertension and electrolyte imbalances associated with these conditions.
